name: Angle-resolved remote overlap

label: eq:contacteq
title: Proof
body_md:
Use the preceding coordinates, with stem $x=y=0$. If $T$ meets the stem at time $\tau$ and contains an observation point $z=(x,y,t)$, put $H=t-\tau$. Up to $O(\delta)$ errors,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:contacteq}
 x=Hu+O(\delta),\qquad y=H|u|^2/2+O(\delta).
\end{equation}
Resolve $|H|\ge h$ into dyadic shells $|H|\sim H_0$. If $H_0\rho\lesssim\delta$, there are at most
$C(1+\rho/\delta)^d\lesssim H_0^{-d}$ possible direction parameters. For each parameter only $O(1)$ spatially separated tubes contain $z$.

Otherwise $|x|\sim H_0\rho$, and \eqref{eq:contacteq} implies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:criticalvalue}
 u=x/H+O(\delta/H_0),\qquad
 \left|y-\frac{|x|^2}{2H}\right|\lesssim\delta.
\end{equation}
On either signed shell, the derivative of
$H\mapsto y-|x|^2/(2H)$ is comparable to $\rho^2$. Thus eligible $H$ occupy an interval of length at most $C\delta/\rho^2$. The corresponding points $x/H$ trace a curve of length at most $C\delta/(H_0\rho)$. Its $C\delta/H_0$-neighborhood is covered by $O(\rho^{-1})$ balls of radius $C\delta/H_0$, each containing at most $O(H_0^{-d})$ members of a $\delta$-separated direction set. Spatial separation again allows only $O(1)$ tubes per direction through $z$. Summing the geometric series in $H_0$ proves \eqref{eq:remote}.

For \eqref{eq:pair}, two center lines with slope difference comparable to $\rho$ can remain within $O(\delta)$ of each other for only $O(\delta/\rho)$ time. Multiply by the spatial cross-sectional volume $O(\delta^{n-1})$.

label: lem:angular
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:angular}
Fix $\eta>0$. Let $\mathcal A$ be $J$ direction labels in a bounded $d$-dimensional patch, with bounded occupancy in each $\delta$-ball. Unless $J\le C_\eta\delta^{-\eta}$, there is a dyadic $\rho\in[\delta,1]$ and two subsets, each of size at least $c_\eta\delta^\eta J$, contained in one $C\rho$-cap and separated by at least $c_\eta\rho$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Maximize $\#(\mathcal A\cap B(u,r))/r^\eta$ over $\delta\le r\le C$. The maximizing ball contains at least $c\delta^\eta J$ labels. Choose $c_1=c_1(\eta)$ with $c_1^\eta<1/4$. Maximality implies that a ball of radius $c_1r$ contains at most one quarter of the maximizing ball's labels, provided $c_1r\ge\delta$. Cover the maximizing ball by boundedly many $c_1r/10$-balls. One contains a fixed $\eta$-dependent fraction of its labels; at least three quarters lie outside the concentric $c_1r$-ball. These are the two separated groups. If $c_1r<\delta$, bounded $\delta$-scale occupancy gives $J\le C_\eta\delta^{-\eta}$. Replacing $r$ by a comparable dyadic number concludes the proof.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The argument does not apply a Lorentz transformation at the dynamically selected scale $\rho$. Only fixed coordinate changes are used. The count of directions in a $\rho$-cap supplies the factor $\rho^d$, which compensates for the angular losses in \eqref{eq:E-lower}. Spatial separation, used in Lemma~\ref{lem:remote}, is also the reason the final dependence is $m^{1/2}$ rather than $m$.
head: environment

label: prop:KT
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the original coordinates $(x,t)$ and project to $x\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. On finitely many patches without antipodal pairs, projected directions are separated, projected tubes have length comparable to one, and the two-ends condition is preserved. The latter holds because projection is uniformly bi-Lipschitz along each center line.

Choose one representative tube per direction. The projected shading of one representative has volume comparable to $\lambda\delta^{n-2}$. The Katz--Tao input in \cite[Theorem~3.5]{WW}, with ambient dimension $n-1$, gives
\[
 |\pi E_Y|\gtrapprox
 \lambda^{(2n+8)/7}\delta^{3(n-2)/7}
             (D\lambda\delta^{n-2})^{4/7}.
\]
Since $E_Y$ is a union of $\delta$-cubes,
$|E_Y|\gtrsim\delta|\pi E_Y|$. Since
$S_Y\lesssim mD\lambda\delta^{n-1}$, division gives \eqref{eq:projected}. Finitely many patches are combined with a fixed loss.
